title: Anytime Algorithms for Approximate Functional Dependencies

problem.claim: Identify approximate functional dependencies in a relation, including finding top-k AFDs and identifying all AFDs within a specified error threshold.

gap.claim: Existing approaches do not provide the proposed anytime framework for producing results after each processed record while estimating error bounds for candidate AFDs.

contributions.claim: A computational framework identifies approximate functional dependencies using frequency distributions of individual attributes without requiring access to the full database.
The framework includes an exact algorithm that provides precise solutions when possible and an algorithm that always returns a solution with some imprecision.
The algorithms support data organization strategies including indexing by key or key-like attributes.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world and synthetic datasets reportedly validate the approach's effectiveness.
The authors report that the approach outperforms state-of-the-art solutions.

narrative_sequence.summary: The work addresses identifying approximate functional dependencies and formalizes top-k and error-threshold problems.
It proposes a framework based on individual-attribute frequency distributions that processes records incrementally without the full database.
It develops anytime solutions, error-bound estimation, an exact algorithm when possible, and an always-returning approximate algorithm.
It evaluates applicability under multiple data organization strategies using real-world and synthetic datasets.
The authors report effectiveness and improved performance over state-of-the-art solutions.

source_observation.claim: The algorithms return results after each processed record and can operate without access to the full database.

interpretation.claim: Incremental, anytime processing can support useful partial results when complete data access or full computation is unavailable.

application.claim: Use progressive algorithms with explicit error bounds for large or streaming data analysis.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when the imprecise algorithm's output is sufficiently accurate or how error bounds behave across data distributions.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quantitative performance results.
The abstract does not specify the exact error-bound formulas or algorithmic complexity.
The abstract does not identify the datasets, baselines, or experimental settings.
